subject: physics
title: Forces and their interactions
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Forces and their interactions — AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification, section 4.5.1.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics (AQA) practice covering Forces and their interactions, specification section 4.5.1.
final_note: You worked through Forces and their interactions — 28 specification statements.

concepts.def: A quantity that has magnitude only. A scalar is fully described by a size and a unit, with no direction attached to it. Mass, speed, distance, energy and time are scalars.
A quantity that has magnitude and an associated direction. A vector is only fully described when both are given. Force, weight, velocity, displacement and acceleration are vectors.

The representation of a vector quantity by an arrow drawn on a diagram. The length of the arrow represents the magnitude of the vector, and the direction the arrow points represents the direction of the vector quantity.

A push or pull that acts on an object due to the interaction with another object. A force is not something an object stores or owns; it exists only while two objects interact, and it is measured in newtons.
A force between two objects that are physically touching. Friction, air resistance, tension and the normal contact force are contact forces.
A force between two objects that are physically separated. Gravitational force, electrostatic force and magnetic force are non-contact forces.
A contact force that acts between two surfaces that are touching, acting along the surfaces and opposing the relative motion, or attempted motion, between them.
A contact force acting on an object moving through air. The object is physically touching the particles of the air, which is why it is classed as a contact force.
A contact force transmitted along a stretched rope, string, cable or spring, pulling on the objects attached at each end of it.
The contact force exerted by a surface on an object that is touching it, acting at right angles (normal) to that surface.
A non-contact force of attraction between two objects that have mass. It acts even though the objects are physically separated, for example between the Earth and an object above its surface.
A non-contact force between electrically charged objects. Like charges repel and opposite charges attract, and the force acts across the space between the charged objects.
A non-contact force between magnets, or between a magnet and a magnetic material, which acts across the gap between them without the objects touching.
The two forces produced when two objects interact. Each object exerts a force on the other, the two forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, and each force acts on a different object.

The force acting on an object due to gravity, measured in newtons, N. Close to the Earth it is due to the gravitational field around the Earth, and it is calculated from weight = mass × gravitational field strength.

The quantity, symbol g, measured in newtons per kilogram, N/kg, that describes the strength of a gravitational field at a point. The weight of an object depends on the gravitational field strength at the point where the object is.

The quantity of matter in an object, symbol m, measured in kilograms, kg. Mass is a scalar quantity and it does not change when the object is moved to a place with a different gravitational field strength.

The single point at which the weight of an object may be considered to act. Treating the weight as one force acting at this point allows an object to be handled as though all of its mass were concentrated there.

A relationship in which one quantity is a fixed multiple of another, so that multiplying one by a number multiplies the other by the same number, and a graph of one against the other is a straight line through the origin. The weight of an object and the mass of an object are directly proportional.
A calibrated spring-balance used to measure weight in newtons. The spring extends more as the force pulling on it increases, and the scale is marked so that the reading gives the weight directly.
The single force that has the same effect as all of the original forces acting on an object together. A number of forces acting on an object may always be replaced by this one force.

A diagram showing a single isolated object or system on its own, with every force acting on that object drawn as an arrow from it. It is used to describe qualitatively how several forces combine to give a resultant force.
Forces on an object that combine to give a resultant force of zero. The individual forces are still acting, but they have no overall effect on the motion of the object.
Replacing a single force by two component forces acting at right angles to each other. The two component forces together have the same effect as the single force they replace.
The situation in which the forces acting on an object are balanced, so the resultant force is zero. On a scale vector diagram the arrows representing the forces form a closed shape.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes a scalar quantity?
options: It is described by a magnitude only, and never by a direction.
It is described by a magnitude and also by a direction.
It is a quantity that does not describe anything moving.
It is described by an arrow that can be any length.
mcqs.explain: Scalar quantities have magnitude only, which is exactly what this states.

mcqs.q: Which statement is true of a vector quantity but not of a scalar quantity?
options: It can be given a size in a unit such as the newton.
It always describes an object that is moving.
It can be shown as a label on a scale diagram.
It has a direction associated with its magnitude.
mcqs.explain: Vector quantities have magnitude and an associated direction, and that direction is what a scalar lacks.

mcqs.q: Two forces are drawn as arrows on the same diagram. One arrow is twice as long as the other. What does this tell you?
options: The two forces are equal, but drawn at two different scales.
The longer arrow was drawn bigger just to look neat.
The force shown by the longer arrow is twice as large.
Arrow length is up to the artist and shows nothing.
mcqs.explain: The length of the arrow represents the magnitude, so a doubled length is a doubled force.

mcqs.q: Which statement best describes what a force is?
options: A property of an object that heavy objects have more of.
Something stored in a moving object and used up later.
A push or pull that acts only when two objects touch.
A push or pull on an object due to another object.
mcqs.explain: A force is a push or pull that acts on an object due to the interaction with another object.

mcqs.q: A crate is dragged across a rough floor. Why is the friction between the crate and the floor a contact force?
options: Because the crate stays right next to the floor below.
Because the crate is also touching the air around it.
Because the crate and the floor are physically touching.
Because the crate rests on the ground, not falling.
mcqs.explain: Contact forces are those where the objects are physically touching, which the crate and floor are.

mcqs.q: The Earth pulls on a satellite high above its surface. Why is this gravitational force a non-contact force?
options: Because there is no air in space to pass the force along.
Because the Earth and the satellite are physically separated.
Because the two objects can never touch one another.
Because the satellite's mass and weight are lower in space.
mcqs.explain: Non-contact forces act between objects that are physically separated, which is the case here.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of a contact force?
options: The tension in a stretched tow-rope
The magnetic force between two bar magnets
The gravitational force on a falling ball
The electrostatic force between charges
mcqs.explain: Tension is listed by the specification as a contact force, alongside friction and air resistance.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of a non-contact force?
options: The air resistance on a falling skydiver
The upthrust on a boat floating on the sea.
The drag on a fish swimming in the water.
The electrostatic force between charges
mcqs.explain: Electrostatic force is listed by the specification as a non-contact force.

mcqs.q: Which pair of forces are both non-contact forces?
options: Magnetic and gravitational forces
Air resistance and electrostatic force
Drag in water and the magnetic force.
Upthrust and a gravitational force.
mcqs.explain: Both are listed by the specification as non-contact forces, acting between separated objects.

mcqs.q: A student writes that the force on a trolley is 12 N. Why is this description incomplete?
options: Because the mass in kilograms was not given too.
Because force is a vector, so a direction is needed.
Because a force in newtons must be converted to kilograms.
Because a vector must also be given a speed.
mcqs.explain: Force is a vector quantity, so a full description gives the magnitude and the direction.

mcqs.q: A tennis ball is struck by a racket. Which statement describes the interaction between them correctly?
options: Only the racket exerts a force, because it moved first of all.
The racket pushes the ball harder than the ball pushes the racket.
Each exerts a force on the other, equal in size and opposite in direction.
Both forces act on the ball, so they cancel and it cannot move.
mcqs.explain: The two objects interact, and the interaction produces a force on each of them, drawn as a pair of vectors.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the weight of a book resting on a shelf is correct?
options: It is the total amount of matter contained in the book.
It is the push of the shelf upwards on the book.
It is a property the book has whatever happens.
It is the force acting on the book due to gravity.
mcqs.explain: Weight is the force acting on an object due to gravity, which close to the Earth is due to its gravitational field.

mcqs.q: An astronaut takes a 3 kg toolbox from the Earth (g = 9.8 N/kg) to the Moon (g = 1.6 N/kg). What happens?
options: Its mass and weight both fall, because gravity is weaker there.
Its mass and weight both drop to about a sixth.
Its mass stays at 3 kg but its weight becomes smaller.
Its mass and its weight do not change on the way there.
mcqs.explain: Mass does not depend on location; weight depends on the gravitational field strength at that point.

mcqs.q: Which equation is used to calculate the weight of an object?
options: weight = mass ÷ the gravitational field strength
weight = mass plus gravitational field strength
mass = weight × gravitational field strength g
weight = mass × gravitational field strength
mcqs.explain: This is the equation exactly as the specification gives it, W = m g.

mcqs.q: A rock has a mass of 12 kg. The gravitational field strength is 9.8 N/kg. What is the weight of the rock?
mcqs.explain: W = m g = 12 × 9.8 = 117.6 N, with weight in newtons.

mcqs.q: A bag has a weight of 49 N at a place where the gravitational field strength is 9.8 N/kg. What is the mass of the bag?
options: 5 kg
0.2 kg
mcqs.explain: Rearranging W = m g gives m = W ÷ g = 49 ÷ 9.8 = 5 kg.

mcqs.q: Which row gives the correct units for the quantities in W = m g?
options: W in newtons, m in kilograms and g in newtons per kilogram
W in kilograms, m in kilograms and g in newtons per kilogram
W in grams, m in kilograms and g in newtons per kilogram
W in newtons, m in kilograms and g in newtons of force
mcqs.explain: These are the units exactly as the specification gives them: N, kg and N/kg.

mcqs.q: What does g stand for in the equation W = m g, and what is its unit?
options: Gravitational field strength, measured in newtons per kilogram
The force of gravity acting on the object, given in newtons
The weight of the object, measured in kilograms.
The strength of gravity there, measured in kilograms
mcqs.explain: The specification gives gravitational field strength, g, in newtons per kilogram, N/kg.

mcqs.q: Why is the weight of an object drawn as a single arrow from one point on it?
options: Because weight acts where the object presses on the surface below.
Because the weight may be taken to act at the centre of mass.
Because gravity only acts on the part touching the ground.
Because a vector must always be drawn from the ground.
mcqs.explain: The weight of an object may be considered to act at a single point, its centre of mass.

mcqs.q: The weight of an object and the mass of an object are directly proportional. What does this mean?
options: Weight increases by a fixed amount each time mass increases.
Doubling the mass doubles the weight in the same field.
Weight just gets bigger by some amount when mass increases.
Weight and mass are equal when the units are ignored.
mcqs.explain: Directly proportional means one quantity is a fixed multiple of the other, so the factor carries across.

mcqs.q: A block of mass 4 kg has a weight of 24 N on a planet. A second block on the same planet has a mass of 12 kg. What is its weight?
options: 32 N, because the extra 8 kg of mass adds another 8 N to the weight.
72 N, because the mass is three times larger and so the weight is too.
2 N, because the mass is divided by the gravitational field strength.
36 N, because the weight goes up by 12 N for each extra block.
mcqs.explain: Weight and mass are directly proportional, so a mass three times larger gives a weight three times larger.

mcqs.q: Which instrument is used to measure the weight of an object?
options: A set of kitchen scales marked in kilograms
An electronic balance reading in kilograms
A spring-balance calibrated in newtons
A balance comparing two known masses
mcqs.explain: Weight is measured using a calibrated spring-balance, also called a newtonmeter.

mcqs.q: What is meant by the resultant force on an object?
options: The largest of all of the forces that are acting on the object.
The force that is left once the object has stopped moving.
The single force with the same effect as all of them together.
The total of the sizes of every force that acts on it.
mcqs.explain: A number of forces may be replaced by a single force with the same effect: the resultant force.

mcqs.q: A box is pulled to the right with a force of 12 N while a friction force of 5 N acts to the left. What is the resultant force?
options: 17 N, acting to the right
12 N acting to the right
7 N acting to the left
7 N acting to the right
mcqs.explain: For forces in a straight line the resultant is 12 - 5 = 7 N, in the direction of the larger force.

mcqs.q: A ball hangs at rest on the end of a string. A free body diagram of the ball is drawn. Which forces should appear on it?
options: The tension in the string and the pull of the ball on the string as well.
The weight of the ball and the pull of the ball on the Earth below.
The weight of the ball and the tension in the string, both acting on the ball.
No forces at all, because the ball is hanging still on the string.
mcqs.explain: A free body diagram shows the isolated object with only the forces that act on it.

mcqs.q: A parachutist falls at a steady speed. Her weight is 700 N. What can be said about the forces on her?
options: The forces cancel out, so really no force acts at all.
Air resistance is 700 N upwards, so the resultant force is zero.
Her weight and the air resistance are an action pair.
No forces act on her now, since her speed is not changing.
mcqs.explain: The forces are balanced: an upward 700 N air resistance and a 700 N weight give a resultant of zero.

mcqs.q: A single force is resolved into two components acting at right angles to each other. Which statement is correct?
options: The two components together have the same effect as the force.
The two components add up numerically to the size of the single force.
Each component is exactly half the size of the original single force.
The two components replace a force that has no direction.
mcqs.explain: The two component forces together have the same effect as the single force they replace.

mcqs.q: Two forces at right angles act on a point. A student draws them to scale, head to tail, to find the resultant. What must the final answer state?
options: The magnitude in newtons only, since that is the number asked for.
The magnitude in newtons and the direction of the force.
The direction only, because a scale drawing cannot give a size.
The magnitude in newtons and the total length of both arrows.
mcqs.explain: The resultant is a vector, so the answer gives both magnitude and direction from the scale drawing.
